title: We copied the 13 top Binance grid bots on 30 Sep. 12 days later only 4 were in profit, but the grids weren't the problem
author: MobileBed8587

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: the coins falling 6% is most of the story. a spot grid buys every step down, so it's long the coin by design, and a top-PNL list picked after a rising stretch mostly ranks who held the most coin. I'd score each bot against just holding its own coin.

replies.author: MobileBed8587
replies.body:
Agreed, and that's exactly the comparison GridCheck makes. The "beat holding" number in the post is each bot vs holding its own coin.

 One refinement: we don't compare against 100% coin, because a grid usually starts part coin, part cash. The baseline is holding the same coin share the grid bought on day one, after fees. Otherwise a grid that started 40% in coin "beats" holding in any falling market just by having less exposure.



 On that like-for-like basis:

 \- 9 of these 13 copied bots are ahead of holding their starting coin share since 30 Sep. That's mostly because the coins fell and the grids started part in cash. It isn't the grid being clever.

 \- Over the previous 60 days, the same 30 top bots' typical launch beat that baseline by −0.15 pp, which is basically just the setup fee. Only 3 of 30 added anything real.

 So yes: the leaderboard mostly ranks coin exposure and timing, not grid skill. The "Grid vs holding" column on the site is that number for every bot: [https://gridcheck.pages.dev/leaders](https://gridcheck.pages.dev/leaders) 

checkout more details on this free dashboard: [https://gridcheck.pages.dev/leaders](https://gridcheck.pages.dev/leaders)

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: holding the same coin share the grid started with is a fairer baseline than all coin, yeah. that version I'd trust.
